subject: Priority: ArborX throughput regression — proposed SLA repair roadmap & legal touchpoints
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia@arborx.io>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: sustained throughput drop impacting inference pipelines

Hi Laura,

We started seeing a sustained throughput regression across our primary inference fleet starting ~03:00 UTC this morning. Requests are queuing and worker utilization is spiking; overall token throughput is ~40% below our baseline and error rate for /generate calls has climbed to ~4.7%. This is hitting production traffic for our recommendation flows.

Can you confirm you’ve seen this on Redwood’s side and what the immediate mitigation plan is? We’re preparing a cross-functional war room and will need an estimate of expected restore time, plus an initial view on commercial remedies if the SLA is impacted.

I’ve attached a short export from our logs (arborx_error_log_snippet.txt).

- Amelia
Amelia Torres
Head of Platform
ArborX
amelia@arborx.io
From: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
To: Amelia Torres <amelia@arborx.io>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained throughput drop impacting inference pipelines

Hi Amelia — thanks for the heads up and for the log snippet. We’re seeing the same signal on our telemetry: a backend autoscaling regression combined with a KV-cache eviction storm for long-running sessions. Engineering is in a hotfix path; I’ve asked Monica (CS lead) and Ben (Commercial) to join the war room.

Immediate next steps (we’ll keep you updated every 30 minutes):
- Engineering: isolate affected clusters and move ARX traffic to a prioritized routing pool (in progress).
- Ops: deploy a targeted config rollback to restore previous batching thresholds (ETA 25m).
- CS: monitor request success rate/latency and validate end-to-end flows.

We understand the business impact and will propose a commercial remedy if the incident is an SLA breach.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, jordan_blake@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: ARX: exec sync needed - potential SLA exposure (catch-up threads inside)

Team —

Status: ARX is experiencing ~40% throughput shortfall for production routes; error rate ~4.7%. Monica confirms mitigation steps are restoring throughput to ~85% of baseline after config rollback. We should prepare:
1) A short exec brief for ARX leadership that explains root cause, timeline, mitigations, and proposed credits.
2) A proposed credit schedule (hours impacted * % of monthly committed throughput) and a contract amendment workflow (legal + DocuSign).
3) A customer-facing remediation / postmortem doc and a follow-up health check cadence.

Ben — can you draft a commercial proposal we can present within 24 hours? Include an initial credit framework and optional accelerated SLA review with Priority remediation. Jordan — if this escalates to execs at ARX, help prep an escalation note and recommended execs to join. Monica — keep the customer comms rhythm and confirm when all services are back at baseline.

I’ll assemble the exec brief for ARX. We should aim to have a concrete offer by tomorrow EOD.

- Laura

On Sun, Dec 6, 2026 at 09:45 AM, monica_patel@redwood.example.com wrote:
> Confirmed: rollback completed at 09:34 PT. Observability shows error rate dropping to 0.9% and token throughput returning. We’ll continue monitoring for 6 hours and run a focused regression test against long sessions.
From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ARX: exec sync needed - potential SLA exposure (commercial proposal draft)

Laura — draft proposal below; attaching a formal matrix (proposed-sla-credit-matrix.xlsx) and the one-page exec brief (exec-brief.pdf).

Summary proposal (for discussion):
- Impact window: 2026-12-06T03:00 UTC — 2026-12-06T09:30 UTC (6.5 hours)
- Confirmed SLA thresholds: committed throughput SLO + availability target 99.5% for priority routes (per contract ARX-ENT schedule A)
- Observed: throughput deficit spikes between 40% drop sustained for 4.5 hours and partial restoration window thereafter; 4.7% 5xx for peak interval.

Commercial remedy options (tiered):
A) Goodwill credit (fast): 15% of monthly committed spend pro-rated for impacted window — no paperwork, immediate credit applied to next invoice.
B) Contract amendment & credit (formal): 20% pro-rated credit for impacted window + 3-month credit cap for remedial shielding; amendment routed via Legal + DocuSign (recommended if ARX requests formal contract change).
C) Make whole + SLA review (escalated): 25% credit pro-rated + 90-day priority remediation path and a one-time discounted upgrade for Dedicated capacity trials. Requires executive sign-off.

Notes: I recommend option B as default; option C to offer if ARX requests exec-level assurance. Tagging Jordan to prep the exec note and C-level invite list for offer C.

Next steps:
- Laura: share the proposal with ARX communication and propose a 45-min commercial call tomorrow (Dec 8) to close.
- Monica: confirm final telemetry windows and include stable performance stamp.
- Ben: will draft the amendment language and a DocuSign packet keyed to ARX deal id.

-ben
From: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
To: Amelia Torres <amelia@arborx.io>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com, jordan_blake@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: ARX remediation proposal & next steps (proposed call + DocuSign path)

Amelia — thanks again for patience while we stabilized your traffic. Below is what we propose as a starting point and an ask to close this this week.

What happened (short):
- A config change to batching thresholds + an unexpected KV-cache eviction pattern caused a sustained throughput regression for priority routes between 03:00–09:30 UTC on Dec 6. We rolled back the config and isolated affected clusters; monitoring shows end-to-end flows are back to baseline as of 10:00 UTC on Dec 6. Full postmortem link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/ARX/throughput-postmortem

Commercial remediation (recommendation):
- Recommendation: Option B (formal contract amendment + pro-rated credit)
  - Calculated credit: 20% pro-rated against committed monthly spend for the impacted window (details in attached spreadsheet).
  - Legal steps: we will route a brief amendment for signature via DocuSign. DocuSign reference: DocuSign: 0a1b2c3d-ARX-amoendment

Operational commitments:
- 90-day follow-up health checks with CS + a dedicated remediation engineer from our runtime team for the first 30 days.
- A joint postmortem call to validate root cause and confirm mitigations — proposed Wed Dec 9, 14:00 PT (please confirm).

If you want an escalated commercial commitment (one-time additional credit + priority remediation lane), we can scope that in a C-level call — Jordan is copied and can help coordinate.

Attachments: proposed-sla-credit-matrix.xlsx (breakdown), exec-brief.pdf, arborx_error_log_snippet.txt

Please let me know if Option B works and if you’d like the DocuSign packet routed to your procurement or legal team. We can get the amendment in your hands within 24 hours once we have a confirmation.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Dec 8, 2026 at 15:10 PM, Amelia Torres <amelia@arborx.io> wrote:
